domain: International Law / Treaty Interpretation / Institutional Authority
topic_summary: Analysis of competing interpretations of the Rome Statute's jurisdictional foundation: whether it establishes universal criminal justice authority or a conditional framework requiring sovereign consent. The interpretive contest alters the Court's authority grounding, jurisdictional scope, and legitimacy claims in practice.

key_entities: Rome Statute (foundational treaty text establishing ICC jurisdiction and procedures)
International Criminal Court (institutional authority claiming jurisdiction over atrocity crimes)
State Parties (signatory states recognizing ICC jurisdiction)
Non-State Parties (states not ratifying, asserting sovereignty shield)
UN Security Council (referral mechanism under Chapter VII authority)
key_tensions: Universal jurisdiction claim vs sovereign consent requirement (universalist vs sovereigntist readings)
Complementarity principle vs primary jurisdiction assertion (ICC deference to national courts vs override authority)
key_mechanisms: Article 12 jurisdiction trigger (territorial state OR national state ratification OR UNSC referral)
Complementarity assessment (unwilling/unable test for national prosecution)
Arrest warrant enforcement (dependent on state cooperation; no independent enforcement capacity)
key_absences: Enforcement mechanism independent of state cooperation (ICC has no police force or military)
Explicit hierarchy resolution between complementarity and universal mandate (Statute text does not prioritize when they conflict)

readings.expected_structural_delta: ICC jurisdiction extends to non-party nationals via territorial or UNSC triggers; victims include all persons regardless of state consent; authority claims override national sovereignty for core crimes

readings.commitment: Rome Statute creates conditional framework requiring strict sovereign consent for jurisdiction
readings.authority_grounding: Westphalian sovereignty / treaty law positivism / consent-based obligation
readings.expected_structural_delta: ICC jurisdiction limited to consenting states; non-party nationals immune except via UNSC referral; national courts retain primary authority; complementarity as deference not override

readings.commitment: Rome Statute balances universal aspiration with sovereign primacy via complementarity mechanism
readings.authority_grounding: Institutional pragmatism / cooperative federalism analogue / progressive realization
readings.expected_structural_delta: ICC has residual universal authority but operationally constrained by complementarity deference; jurisdiction exists but enforcement depends on state cooperation; authority grounded in hybrid of natural law aspiration and treaty consent

axiom_contradictions.basis: No single framework can simultaneously hold that crimes against humanity create jurisdiction independent of state consent AND that state consent is prerequisite for jurisdiction; one axiom requires accepting jurisdiction as inherent to crime commission, the other requires accepting jurisdiction as derivative of treaty ratification

omegas.description: Does the complementarity principle (Article 17) function as constraint on ICC authority (sovereigntist implication) or as temporary deference pending national failure (universalist implication)? Statute text does not explicitly resolve hierarchy when universal mandate and complementarity conflict. Hybrid reading attempts mediation but may collapse under operational pressure.
omegas.source: Extraction absence: no explicit hierarchy resolution in Statute text; tension between universal aspiration and sovereign primacy

omegas.description: Article 12(2)(a) territorial jurisdiction trigger allows prosecution of non-party nationals if crime occurs on party state territory. Does this constitute universal jurisdiction bootstrapping (universalist claim) or legitimate territorial sovereignty exercise (sovereigntist claim)? Interpretive ambiguity allows both readings to cite same provision as support.
omegas.source: Dark Matter Probe 3 (Beneficiary Scan): textual ambiguity benefits ICC institutional expansion while preserving sovereigntist challenge pathway

omegas.description: If enforcement gap persists (deferred mountain constraint), does this collapse hybrid_complementarity_reading toward sovereigntist_reading over time? Inability to enforce warrants against non-cooperating states may erode universalist claims through demonstrated impotence rather than legal argument.
omegas.source: Downstream interaction between deferred enforcement_gap_constraint and selected readings; operational reality may drive interpretive drift

omegas.description: The axiom contradiction between universalist and sovereigntist readings produces licensed plurality: both are socially live positions defended by credible authorities. Does this plurality indicate productive interpretive contest or delegitimizing foundational incoherence? Answer may depend on whether ICC institutional performance converges practice toward one reading or maintains permanent bifurcation.
omegas.source: Axiom Contradictions declaration; readings coexist_with edge but contradictory axioms
